Maintenance Report — MNT-0084-009

Asset: WELL-0084 (SW-24 Well 084, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 15 Mar 2024 08:00 · Finished: 20 Mar 2024 04:00 · Well stopped for this job: 116 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Megan Ward Triggered by: inspection INS-0084-0074 on 2024-03-14 Report written: 21 Mar 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that the motor breaker kept tripping and the pump jack would not run. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0084-0074 showed the wellhead at 20.6 °C with the air at 17.3 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. An insulation test showed a winding fault, so the motor was replaced with an exchange unit. The well stayed shut in for about 3 days longer than the repair itself because the job had to wait for a weekday contractor slot.

Root cause

Moisture got into the motor terminal box and damaged the windings.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 2 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Disconnected and removed the motor.
  2. Fitted the exchange motor on the existing base.
  3. Aligned the sheaves and tensioned the belts.
  4. Checked rotation direction and motor current.

Summary of the fix: replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours; motor current within the nameplate rating and stroke rate normal. The well was returned to production.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0084-015

Asset: WELL-0084 (SW-24 Well 084, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: rod string Work started: 30 Nov 2024 08:00 · Finished: 07 Jan 2025 21:00 · Well stopped for this job: 925 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Daniel Foster Triggered by: inspection INS-0084-0109 on 2024-11-28 Report written: 07 Jan 2025

What happened

Field staff reported that the operator noticed the pump jack running unusually light and no fluid reaching the flowline. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0084-0109 showed the wellhead at 17.7 °C with the air at 13.1 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A dynamometer card showed no load from the downhole pump, which points to a parted rod. The company workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 37 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Root cause

Fatigue failure of a rod body, probably started by corrosion pitting.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rod string and located the break.
  3. Recovered the lower section with an overshot fishing tool.
  4. Replaced the damaged rods.
  5. Ran the rod string back in and spaced out the pump.

Summary of the fix: fished and replaced parted rod section.

Testing and return to service

Pump test showed normal fluid delivery and the rod load returned to normal. The well was returned to production.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0084-032

Asset: WELL-0084 (SW-24 Well 084, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 19 Sep 2026 08:00 · Finished: 07 Oct 2026 03:00 · Well stopped for this job: 427 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Megan Ward · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0084-0203 on 2026-09-17 Report written: 09 Oct 2026

What happened

Field staff reported that oil was dripping from the gearbox onto the pump jack base. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0084-0203 showed the wellhead at 33.0 °C with the air at 28.4 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The input shaft seal was worn and the gearbox oil level was below the sight glass. The well stayed shut in for about 16 days longer than the repair itself because the crew was committed to a higher-priority spill response elsewhere in the field.

Root cause

Seal wear, made worse by heat and a low oil level.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Drained the gearbox oil into a closed container.
  2. Replaced the input and output shaft seals.
  3. Cleaned the base and absorbed the spilled oil.
  4. Refilled with the specified gear oil to the correct level.

Summary of the fix: replaced gearbox seals and topped up oil.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 1 hour and checked both shafts for leaks: none found. The well was returned to production.

Waste

  • Used gear oil and oily pads sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0084-032 (WS-06).
